name: sealed_sheet_budget_lam125
_purpose: EXPLORATORY (design track; TASKS T13 rung 3). A sealed box is a black hole: nothing leaves. Give a perfect sheet of space a fixed budget of energy it cannot get rid of, and see whether the energy re-curls the space (the author's black hole) or melts it ([T25]'s).
_prediction_written_before_the_run: Curling is the cheaper damage: at lambda = 1.25 an extra square on a full edge costs 4 and a destroyed square costs 16, so per square curling is four times cheaper. Predicted: at small budgets (0.5 to 2 per point) the damage is mostly curled, vertices at d = 1 and 0, with few melted ones; as the budget rises the melted count overtakes it, and by 8 to 16 per point the sheet is mostly melted. If instead melted vertices dominate at every budget, concentrated energy in this model makes a random bubble and not a fold, which is [T25]'s black hole and against the author's.
